title: Improving the School Canteen
description: Practise passives, formal linking and wish, then write a proposal for improving your school canteen.
instructions: Do the exercises in Part 1. Then write your text in Part 2.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: At the moment, all meals ___ in the kitchen of another school.
exercises.explanation: Use the present simple passive (am/is/are + past participle) for current routines when the doer is not the focus.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the word in brackets.
exercises.text: It is recommended that more vegetarian dishes ___ (offer) from next term.
answers: be offered
should be offered
exercises.explanation: After "recommend that" in formal English, use the subjunctive (be offered) or should + passive infinitive (should be offered).

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: The salad bar is popular, whereas the desserts are rarely chosen.
The desserts are rarely chosen, whereas the salad bar is popular.
exercises.explanation: "Whereas" joins two contrasting facts in one sentence.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: Many students wish the canteen would be open earlier yesterday.
answers: Many students wish the canteen had been open earlier yesterday.
exercises.explanation: For regret about the past (yesterday), use wish + past perfect: wish the canteen had been open.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: The queues are very long. ___, many students eat nothing at lunchtime.
exercises.explanation: "Consequently" shows a result: the long queues cause students to skip lunch.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the word in brackets. You may add one linking word.
exercises.text: ___ (ask) about the menu, most students said it was too repetitive.
answers: When asked
Asked
exercises.explanation: A past participle clause (Asked ... / When asked ...) has a passive meaning: when the students were asked.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word given and do not change it. Use between two and five words, including the word given. Second sentence: "A new water fountain ___ next month."
exercises.text: The school will install a new water fountain next month.
answers: A new water fountain will be installed next month.
A new water fountain will be installed by the school next month.
exercises.explanation: The future passive is will + be + past participle: will be installed.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word given and do not change it. Use between two and five words, including the word given. Second sentence: "If so many students had ___ out of food."
exercises.text: The canteen ran out of food because so many students came.
answers: If so many students had not come, the canteen would not have run out of food.
If so many students had not come, the canteen wouldn't have run out of food.
exercises.explanation: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would (not) have + past participle, for an unreal past situation.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: The chef ___ forgotten to add salt; the soup has no taste at all.
exercises.explanation: Must have + past participle is a confident deduction about the past, based on evidence.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the word in brackets.
exercises.text: Students often complain about the lack of ___ (vary) on the menu.
answers: variety
exercises.explanation: The noun formed from vary is variety (a range of different things).

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: The school had the canteen repainted last summer.
Last summer the school had the canteen repainted.
The school had repainted the canteen last summer.
exercises.explanation: Causative have + object + past participle shows that someone else did the work: had the canteen repainted.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: Most students would like to have a healthier food.
answers: Most students would like to have healthier food.
Most students would like to have some healthier food.
exercises.explanation: Food is uncountable here, so it cannot take a/an.

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word given and do not change it. Use between two and five words, including the word given. Second sentence: "We ___ packed lunches."
exercises.text: It wasn't necessary for us to bring packed lunches, but we did.
answers: We needn't have brought packed lunches.
exercises.explanation: Needn't have + past participle means you did something, but it was not necessary.

exercises.focus: Formal linking: on the other hand
exercises.prompt: Choose the correct answer.
exercises.text: The new menu is healthier. ___, it is more expensive.
exercises.explanation: On the other hand starts a new sentence and introduces a contrasting point.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the word in brackets.
exercises.text: The cook explained that the oven ___ (break) down the previous day.
answers: had broken
exercises.explanation: In reported speech, an earlier past action moves back to the past perfect: had broken.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in the correct order to make a sentence.
answers: Most students would rather eat outside than in the canteen.
Most students would rather eat in the canteen than outside.
exercises.explanation: Would rather + infinitive without to ... than expresses a preference.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: The queue was such long that we missed the start of the lesson.
answers: The queue was so long that we missed the start of the lesson.
exercises.explanation: Use so before an adjective on its own (so long); use such before a noun phrase (such a long queue).

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word given and do not change it. Use between two and five words, including the word given. Second sentence: "The canteen ___ to seat all the students."
exercises.text: The canteen is so small that it can't seat all the students.
answers: The canteen is not big enough to seat all the students.
The canteen is not large enough to seat all the students.
exercises.explanation: Not + adjective + enough + to-infinitive means something lacks the necessary quality.

exercises.prompt: There is one mistake in the sentence. Write the correct sentence.
exercises.text: There didn't use to be any vegetarian options, but now there is several.
answers: There didn't use to be any vegetarian options, but now there are several.
exercises.explanation: With there + be, the verb agrees with the noun that follows: there are several (options).

exercises.prompt: Complete the second sentence so that it means the same as the first. Use the word given and do not change it. Use between two and five words, including the word given. Second sentence: "The school ___ every morning."
exercises.text: A catering company delivers the school's meals every morning.
answers: The school has its meals delivered every morning.
The school has its meals delivered by a catering company every morning.
The school has the meals delivered every morning.
The school has its meals delivered by the catering company every morning.
exercises.explanation: Causative have + object + past participle shows that a service is done by someone else.

task.prompt: Your head teacher wants to improve the school canteen and has asked students for proposals. Write a proposal for the head teacher.
contentPoints: Describe the current situation in the canteen.
Explain the main problems students have mentioned.
Make at least two practical recommendations.
Explain how the changes would benefit students.
usefulLanguage: The aim of this proposal is to ...
task.modelAnswer:
Introduction

The aim of this proposal is to suggest ways of improving the school canteen. It is based on a survey of 120 students which was carried out last month.

Current situation

At present, the canteen serves around 400 meals every day between 12.30 and 1.15. Most dishes are prepared in advance and reheated, and the menu changes only once a month.

Main problems

When asked about the canteen, most students complained about the long queues. Many of them said that they had sometimes missed lunch altogether because the break was too short. In addition, the food is considered unhealthy and repetitive, whereas students would like more fresh and vegetarian options.

Recommendations

Firstly, it is recommended that lunch be served in two shifts, so that younger and older students eat at different times. Secondly, a salad bar should be introduced, and the menu should be changed every week. Finally, a suggestion box could be placed near the entrance.

Conclusion

If these changes were made, queues would become shorter and students would eat more healthily. Consequently, they would feel more energetic in afternoon lessons. I strongly believe that the proposal would benefit the whole school community.
